BIBTRAIN \- List of Suggested Topics

Please describe the topic of the training material you are suggesting and add it to one individual category (or more) described in this general workflow (cf. schema below): [https\://marketplace.sshopencloud.eu/workflow/tE2HiC](https://marketplace.sshopencloud.eu/workflow/tE2HiC)

**Training Material 1**

**Topic:** Bibliodata formats and standards

**Author:** Vojtěch Malínek

**Classification:** Data Acquisition / Analysis

**Short description:** The aim of the training material is to introduce existing bibliodata standards and formats (MARC formats, BIBFRAME, ISBD, RDA etc.) and their specific parameters which helps the interested audience to better understand the context and content of bibliographical data. Simultaneously, the specificities of bibliographic and authority data will be discussed.

**Training Material 2**

**Topic:** Documentation and data paper preparation for bibliodatasets

**Author:** Nanette Rißler-Pipka

**Classification:** Data management / Documentation / Dissemination 

**Short description:** The aim of the training material is to show different ways to plan your bibliodata project \- addressing the future users of the published datasets, fostering re-use. We introduce data management plan tools for preparing documentation and data papers or datasheets for cultural heritage data \- according to existing templates provided by Europeana and DMP-questionnaires. The support of this task by LLMs will be integrated where useful.  

**Training Material 3**

**Topic:** Retrieving bibliographic records

**Author:** Péter Király

**Classification:** Data Acquisition

**Short description:** The chapter describes different ways to retrieve bibliographic records. It covers file downloads, standard APIs (OAI-PMH, SRU), and screen scraping. It will provide an introduction, and explained code examples (in Python). The chapter also provides downloadable working scripts and/or Jupyter notebooks, and list of data sources (files, API endpoints) as part of an appendix.

**Training Material 4**

**Topic**: Agentic workflows for bibliodata

**Author**: Giovanni Colavizza, Matteo Romanello, anyone else who wants to join

**Classification**: several apply

**Short description**: We consider one bibliodata workflow as an example use case. It could be reference parsing and linkage in the SSH. The material provides a description and implementation of an agentic workflow to achieve this task. It also takes the opportunity to introduce agentic programming concepts, such as tools, skills, hooks. Finally, the material discussed best practices to design agent orchestration workflows for bibliodata.

**Training Material 5**

**Topic**: Automatic bibliographic data extraction with the SSH Citation Index API

**Author**: Matteo Romanello, Giovanni Colavizza

**Classification**: Data preprocessing, data enrichment

**Short description**: This module introduces the SSH Citation Index API, an LLM-powered modular service for bibliographic data preprocessing and enrichment in Social Sciences and Humanities publications. Participants will learn to use its two core endpoints — reference extraction/parsing and citation linking against OpenCitations, Wikidata, OpenAlex, and Matilda — and understand how the pipeline handles SSH-specific challenges (e.g., multilingual sources, footnote citations).

**Training Material 6**

**Topic:** Statistical programming for bibliographic data science 

**Author:** Leo Lahti, Ville Laitinen, Julia Matveeva, Jeba Akewak et al.

**Classification:** Preprocessing, Harmonization, Validation, Analysis

**Short description:** This module demonstrates how statistical programming can be used as a reproducible method to enhance data processing, harmonization, integration, validation, and analysis. Systematically refined bibliographic records are combined with a case study in statistical analysis of open access bibliographic data. 

**Training Material 7**

**Topic:** Refinement, evaluation and publication workflow for bibliography metadata

**Author:** Mikko Tolonen, Eetu Mäkelä, Ville Vaara, Iiro Tiihonen

**Classification:** Harmonization, Validation, Dissemination

**Short description:** We present a workflow for harmonizing, validating, and publishing a bibliographic metadata dataset as an example of a generalizable data refinement process. The focus is on developing a repeatable and extensible workflow for producing research-ready datasets and for assessing the quality of the refinement process. The article provides clear, step-by-step guidance for applying the approach to comparable raw datasets, along with access to the refinement scripts that can serve as a starting point for replicating and adapting the workflow.

**Training Material 8**

 

**Topic:** Data analysis and visualisation

**Author:** Peter Verhaar and anyone else who wants to join

**Classification:** Analysis and dissemination

**Short description:** This tutorial focuses on data visualisation using Python and introduces practical techniques for exploring and presenting bibliographic datasets. The focus is on creating network graphs to analyse relationships and connections between entities, as well as how to build interactive maps for displaying geographic data. Through hands-on examples and widely used Python libraries, the tutorial demonstrates how visualisation can help to uncover patterns and to communicate research findings.

**Training Material 9**

**Topic:** Exploring Citations with OpenCitations API

**Author:** Mario Petrella, Ivan Heibi, Silvio Peroni, Chiara di Giambattista, Arcangelo Massari

**Classification:** Documentation

**Short description:** The aim of this training is to show an expert audience how to use the OpenCitations APIs to retrieve citations and their metadata. This guide is meant as a starting point to introduce the many features the OpenCitations APIs offer. We mainly want to focus on what a typical user does with one of their publications. They usually start by checking how many citations it has, and then they want to see who is actually citing it, along with the related metadata.

**Training Material 10**

**Topic: Exploring Bibliographic Metadata and Texts with AVOBMAT: An Introduction to Critical Text Mining**

**Author:** Róbert Péter

**Classification:** Preprocessing, Enrichment, Analysis

**Short description:**  This hands-on module introduces AVOBMAT's workflow for searching, analysing and visualising bibliographic metadata and texts. Using public digital humanities collections, learners practise corpus selection, metadata networks, n-grams, word-frequency analysis and KWIC, while critically assessing metadata enrichment, text normalisation, analytical settings and reproducibility.
